subject: Plan composition workshop — lean + burst options for MedBridge

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Plan composition workshop — lean + burst options for MedBridge

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. We’re trying to decide between a steady throughput plan (lean) vs a smaller reserved pool plus burst credits for peak days (burst). The key constraints from procurement: predictable monthly spend for budgeting, and a single PO/contract if possible.

Quick background: we estimate ~120M tokens/month steady, with up to 3x spikes 3-4 times a month for scheduled batch jobs. Data residency in US only.

Can you help clarify:
- Which plan better balances predictable spend vs cost savings for spikes?
- Any recommended feature bundles we should include (KV cache, prefix caching, priority routing)?
- What discounts are typical for a 12- vs 24-month commit and for customers with predictable seasonal spikes?

I attached a small usage snapshot (medbridge_usage_snapshot.csv). Would appreciate a short rundown and cost ballpark before we loop in procurement.

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Torres
Product Ops, MedBridge
elena.torres@medbridge.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan composition workshop — lean + burst options for MedBridge

Elena —

Thanks for the usage snapshot, that helps a lot. Short answers up front:
- For your profile (steady base + predictable spikes) our recommended pattern is "Reserved Lite + Burst Credits." Reserved Lite gives predictable baseline capacity and a unit-price anchor for budgeting; burst credits handle the 3x spikes without over-provisioning.
- Feature-wise: enable prefix/KV caching (saves ~15-30% token cost on repeated prompts), priority routing for critical job windows, and the optional high-throughput quantization profile for batch jobs.
- Discounting: typical list discounts vary by commit length. Ballpark: ~15–20% for a 12-month revenue commit, ~22–30% for 24 months depending on upfront vs monthly billing. We can discuss tradeoffs (higher % for upfront).

I want to avoid over-committing capacity you won’t use. Proposed next step: 30-min plan workshop this week to review a 2-option commercial proposal (Lean-reserved vs Reserved+Burst) and walk procurement through the PO/contract flow. Ben, can you draft two side-by-side options with rough pricing and the discount ladders? Lauren, can you flag any legal/contract items to preempt procurement questions (SLA, termination, billing cadence)?

Proposed times: Wed 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 13:00–13:30 PT. What works for you?

—Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, West
Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medbridge.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan composition workshop — lean + burst options for MedBridge

Elena, Vivek —

Thanks — I put together two commercial sketches (see summary below). Full pricing deck attached (redwood_pricing_deck_v3.pdf) and I dropped the hubspot link in the thread. Numbers are estimates until we confirm steady tokens and spike window durations.

Option A — Lean Reserved
- Capacity: Reserved pool sized for 120M tokens/mo steady (covers baseline).
- Add-ons: KV/prefix cache included. Priority routing optional.
- Pricing: list $0.0038/token (reserved rate) -> Monthly estimated $456K.
- Discount: 12mo commit 18% -> $374K/mo; 24mo commit 26% -> $337K/mo.
- Pros: Predictable bill, simpler contract.
- Cons: Higher cost during spikes if you scale reserved pool to peak.

Option B — Reserved Lite + Burst Credits (Recommended)
- Capacity: Reserved Lite sized for ~80M tokens/mo (baseline) + per-month burst credits to cover 3x spikes.
- Add-ons: KV/prefix cache, priority routing for scheduled batch windows, batch quantization profile for jobs.
- Pricing: reserved rate $0.0042/token for Lite; burst token rate (consumed from credits) effective $0.0026/token (pre-purchase credits).
- Example spend (est): baseline ~$336K/mo + burst credits (4 events) ~$60K/mo -> $396K/mo list.
- Discount: 12mo commit 16% -> $333K/mo; 24mo commit 24% -> $301K/mo.
- Pros: Lower total cost for your spike profile, more flexible.
- Cons: Slightly less predictable month-to-month if burst usage varies.

Commercial notes:
- We can lock a cap on monthly overage spend for finance comfort.
- Upfront prepayment reduces effective rate; we can show scenarios.
- Pilot: 6-week pilot at pilot pricing (20% off list) applies, convert or apply credit to committed term if you proceed.

Next steps: Elena, pick a time for the workshop and we’ll bring a one-page MAU/commit worksheet. I linked the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567 and the draft deck.

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan composition workshop — lean + burst options for MedBridge

Ben / Vivek —

Thanks — that framing is exactly what procurement needs. Quick confirmations before the workshop:
1) Can you include a sample clause for an "overage cap" (monthly overage not to exceed X% of committed spend) so we can show legal something in the call?
2) For the pilot -> committed conversion, can pilot credits be applied dollar-for-dollar to the first committed invoice?
3) We prefer monthly billing but with the option to prepay a quarter in advance.

We’ll take the Thu 13:00–13:30 PT slot. I’ll invite procurement (VP Procurement, Javier Morales) to the workshop — looping him in will speed the PO. Also please send a DocuSign version of the commercial term sheet after the workshop.

Happy to run the workshop agenda if you want: 1) usage and spike windows, 2) option walkthrough, 3) overage caps and billing cadence, 4) pilot conversion mechanics, 5) next steps & timeline.

Best,
Elena
